subject: backtransforming to remove bending of specimens

messages.author: 06c72fc2e70ccfe4
messages.subject: backtransforming to remove bending of specimens
parts:
Hello all,
I am trying remove the effects of specimen bending in my landmarks by removing the PC that describes the bending, and then backtransforming to get adjusted coordinates, as in these papers: https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1558-5646.2007.00259.x,  https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1558-5646.2012.01622.x.  This is my first time attempting this, but the way I've found to do it seems to be: X = Z•t(V) + mean(V) where X is the backtransformed data, Z is the PCs (minus the PC being removed), and V is the eigenvectors (minus the one being removed).

My question is how do I get V from the gm.prcomp output, if this is possible? I initially expected from the documentation that V would be the $rotation matrix, but it has a different number of columns from $x, so Z and V are non-conformable and can't be multiplied.

For reference, my landmark array is [24 x 2 x 51], $x is [51 x 46], and $rotation is [48 x 48], and the line I am trying to use to execute the above formula is: pca$x%*%t(pca$rotation)+rowMeans(pca$rotation).

thanks very much in advance,
Grant

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] backtransforming to remove bending of specimens
parts:
Grant,

You have one of two choices.  You can append columns of 0s to V and Z to make it have the same number of columns as X, or better, set tol = 0 as an argument in gm.prcomp.  (Note, gm.prcomp uses RRPP::ordinate to perform ordinations.  The arguments from the ordinate function can, therefore, be adjusted.  See the help file for ordinate to understand more about adjusting dimensions.)

The defaults for gm.prcomp (and ordinate) shave off redundant dimensions, which is a result of size, orientation, position, and possibly autocorrelation of semilandmarks in GPA producing a data space that has fewer dimensions than one might expect based on the number of Cartesian coordinates.  In order to make the math work, you need to retain these redundant dimensions.  Setting tol = 0 will allow that.

Hope that helps.  Good luck!

Mike

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] backtransforming to remove bending of specimens
parts:
Is it possible you have fewer specimens than you have Cartesian coordinates?  The number of PCs with positive eigen values is equal to the minimum of n - 1 and p, for n specimens and p variables.  If p > n -1, your attempted solution might not work.

Another alternative is to use the shape.predictor function.  Here is a way to set it up, using the plethodon example data:

> data("plethodon")
>  Y.gpa <- gpagen(plethodon$land)      
>  PCA <- gm.prcomp(Y.gpa$coords)
>  PC <- PCA$x[,2:4] # using only a portion of the PCs
>  preds <- lapply(1:nrow(PC), function(x) PC[x,])
>  coords <- shape.predictor(Y.gpa$coords, PC, pred1 = PC[1,]) 
> 
>  coords
$pred1
             X             Y
1   0.17557957 -0.0121338710
2   0.20037368 -0.0785753214
3  -0.03263473  0.0009567275
4  -0.28136252 -0.0954307492
5  -0.31250073 -0.0639784607
6  -0.32728420 -0.0409388147
7  -0.32490812  0.0361203464
8  -0.19041459  0.1003581373
9   0.02266422  0.1049202615
10  0.19380144  0.0826135891
11  0.34293524  0.0645293045
12  0.53375074 -0.0984411492
attr(,"class")
[1] "mshape" “matrix"

> Y.gpa$coords[,,1]
             X            Y
1   0.18674483 -0.026016500
2   0.21065409 -0.092572114
3  -0.03230657  0.005234721
4  -0.27638998 -0.087842818
5  -0.31497272 -0.058779020
6  -0.31749593 -0.049605612
7  -0.34224901  0.041577498
8  -0.17653763  0.109650872
9   0.01698938  0.103374558
10  0.18676171  0.071420449
11  0.31041206  0.081513449
12  0.54838978 -0.097955481

You will notice that the coords are changed using only some PCs, but not remarkably.  Unfortunately, as you can see, this would be a one by one solution for specimen coordinates, but one could rig the function to do every specimen.  Here is one way.


>  preds <- lapply(1:nrow(PC), function(x) PC[x,]) # makes a list of specimen PC scores
>  make.prediction <- function(x) shape.predictor(Y.gpa$coords, PC, pred = x)
>  coords <- sapply(preds, make.prediction)
>  coords <- simplify2array(coords)

Maybe this will work for you, and it uses a similar solution via regression.

Mike
